correctness.rationale: Each Blaschke factor has strictly positive boundary argument derivative P_a, the Poisson kernel with mean one; thus |B'|=P_a+P_b and the speed has mean two, also for repeated or zero zeros. Fourier pairing gives the pair integral ∫P_a P_b dθ/(2π)=(1−|a conjugate(b)|²)/|1−a conjugate(b)|², yielding the frozen variance formula. After rotation and interchange write a=r, |b|=t≤r. At fixed t>0 the pair integral uniquely minimizes when its denominator is greatest, i.e. b=−t. The resulting objective is F_r(t)=2[r²/(1−r²)+t²/(1−t²)−2rt/(1+rt)]. Its second derivative is 4[(1+3t²)/(1−t²)³+2r²/(1+rt)³]>0; its first derivative is negative at 0 and positive at r. Thus both endpoints are excluded and the unique global minimum is at the stated root. Comparing s/(1−s²)², strictly increasing in s, to r/(1+rs)², strictly increasing in r at fixed s, verifies strict monotonicity. The root equation has nonzero s-derivative at (0,0) and is invariant under simultaneous sign reversal, so the local branch is analytic and odd. The r³ and r⁵ coefficients follow from A+2=−2 and C+4A+1=1−4A, hence A=−4 and C=32. At r→1 the monotone limit solves L=(1−L)², since 1+L is positive, giving (3−sqrt(5))/2. This verifies the sharp value and all equality cases without running the supplied diagnostic script.

value.rationale: Degree two is the first covering with a choice of how two Poisson-kernel speed contributions can balance. Fixing the outermost radius prevents the constant-speed z² map and fixes how close a zero may come to the boundary. The answer gives a sharp global comparison against the natural equiradial antipodal baseline: that baseline always loses, and the optimum inner zero approaches a precise radius strictly inside the disk even as the prescribed outer zero tends to the boundary. This is a complete, motivated extremal classification and boundary law, rather than just a restatement of Parseval or a one-parameter numerical gain.
